info.name: Food Surplus API
info.description:
Food Surplus platform API — auth, food categories, and admin.

=== SETUP ===
1. Set `base_url` if the API is not on http://127.0.0.1:8000/api
2. Run any Register or Login request — the token is saved into the `token` variable automatically, so every other request just works.

=== RESPONSE SHAPE ===
Every response, success or error, looks like this:
{ "success": bool, "data": object|null, "message": string|null, "errors": object|null }

So you can write ONE response handler for the whole app:
- success == true  -> read `data`
- success == false -> show `message`, and on 422 show `errors` under each field

Status codes: 200 OK · 201 Created · 401 Unauthenticated · 403 Forbidden · 404 Not found · 422 Validation error · 429 Too many requests.

=== ENUMS (fixed values — never send anything else) ===

1) account_type — which kind of account to create (register only)
   "donor"   -> a person/business giving away surplus food
   "charity" -> an organization that collects and distributes it

2) type — the donor's kind. REQUIRED when account_type = "donor"
   "individual" -> a private person
   "restaurant" -> a restaurant
   "hotel"      -> a hotel
   "company"    -> a company

3) status — the charity's account state. READ-ONLY (the API sets it, you only display it)
   "pending"   -> just registered, waiting for the admin. Can log in, but every charity feature returns 403.
   "active"    -> approved by the admin. Full access.
   "suspended" -> blocked by the admin. Can log in to see this, but no access.
   => After login, if data.type == "charity", branch on data.user.status to pick the screen.

4) data.type — which kind of account just logged in (returned by register / login / me)
   "donor" | "charity"  -> use it to decide which home screen to open.

Booleans are real JSON booleans (true/false), not 0/1 or "true".
Times are "HH:MM:SS" (e.g. "08:00:00"). Dates are ISO 8601 UTC.

=== HEADS UP: RATE LIMIT ===
/register and /login accept only 5 requests per minute per IP. Going over returns 429 "Too many requests". If registration suddenly stops working while testing, that is why — wait a minute and continue. Nothing is broken.

request.description:
Creates a donor account. Usable immediately — no admin approval needed.

FIELDS
- account_type : "donor"  (fixed)
- name         : max 120 chars
- type         : "individual" | "restaurant" | "hotel" | "company"   <- dropdown in the UI
- email        : must not exist as a donor OR a charity
- phone        : max 20 chars
- password     : min 8 chars
- password_confirmation : must match password

RETURNS a token — save it and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every protected request.

Note: re-running this returns 422 (email taken). Change the `donor_email` variable to register again.

response.name: 422 Email already taken

request.description:
Creates a charity account. It always starts as status = "pending".

IMPORTANT FOR THE APP FLOW
A pending charity CAN log in and call /me — so it can see its own status — but it CANNOT use any charity feature until an admin approves it. Show a "waiting for approval" screen while status is "pending".

FIELDS
- account_type     : "charity"  (fixed)
- name             : max 120 chars
- email            : must not exist as a donor OR a charity
- phone            : max 20 chars
- password         : min 8 chars
- password_confirmation : must match password
- has_kitchen      : true | false  <- true means it can cook raw food. A charity with false is NEVER shown food that needs cooking.
- address          : max 255 chars
- work_start       : "HH:MM" 24h, e.g. "08:00"
- work_end         : "HH:MM" 24h, must be after work_start
- license_document : optional, send null or omit it

RETURNS status = "pending" plus a token (usable for /me and /logout right away).

response.name: 422 Missing charity fields

request.description:
ONE login endpoint for both account types — do not ask the user whether they are a donor or a charity, the API works it out.

HOW TO ROUTE AFTER LOGIN
1. Read `data.type`:
   "donor"   -> open the donor home screen
   "charity" -> go to step 2
2. For a charity, read `data.user.status`:
   "active"    -> charity home screen
   "pending"   -> "waiting for admin approval" screen
   "suspended" -> "account suspended" screen

A pending or suspended charity logs in successfully (200) on purpose, so it can see where it stands.

BODY: email, password. Wrong email or wrong password both return the same 401 "Invalid credentials" — deliberate, so nobody can discover which emails exist.

request.description:
Returns the currently authenticated donor or charity.

Use this on app start: if the saved token still returns 200, skip the login screen. A 401 means the token is gone or was revoked — send the user back to login.
Revokes only the token used for this request, so signing out on one device does not sign the user out everywhere else. Delete the token from local storage after this succeeds.

The list that fills the food-category dropdown on the "create donation request" screen. Short and fixed, so it is NOT paginated — `data` is a plain array.

Each item has both `name_ar` and `name_en`; show `name_ar` in the Arabic UI.

`default_needs_cooking` is a suggestion, not a rule: when the donor picks a category, pre-fill the "needs cooking?" switch from this value but let them change it. It matters because food that needs cooking is never shown to a charity without a kitchen.

response.name: 200 OK

item.name: Admin
item.description:
Admin endpoints. These do NOT use a Bearer token — they use the static `X-Admin-Token` header instead.

Set the `admin_token` collection variable to the ADMIN_TOKEN value from the backend .env before running these. The value is deliberately left empty here so it never gets committed to the repository.

query.description: Optional: pending | active | suspended. Remove to list all.

request.description:
Lists charities, newest first, paginated 15 per page. Each row includes `strikes_count` (no-show count).

The response `data` is Laravel's paginator object — the actual rows are in `data.data`, and `data.current_page` / `data.last_page` / `data.total` drive pagination.

request.description:
Sets the charity status to `active` so it can start using charity features.

Also used to reinstate a suspended charity — in that case its strikes are cleared, so a single later no-show does not immediately re-suspend it.
